stem:
Omar uses a circuit tester with a cell, a bulb, and wires. He joins aluminium between the free ends and the bulb glows. The tester wires have rubber covering. He also has a piece of dull copper.

Which claims are correct? One or more options may be correct.

options.text: Aluminium is a good conductor of electricity because the bulb glows when the tester circuit is complete.
Touching live metal parts is unsafe because metals that make the tester bulb glow can conduct electricity.
Aluminium is a poor conductor because in another try the bulb stayed off when a tester wire was disconnected.
Dull copper must be a poor conductor because it is not shiny.

teacher.key_rationale: A complete tester that lights shows the joined material conducts; that is why metals that light the bulb are unsafe to touch on live parts. A disconnected wire does not prove aluminium is a poor conductor, and shininess is not the conductivity test.
